main_concerns.concern: The strongest remaining weakness is self-referential validation: the boundary scanner, the open-loop gate, and the E2E retention proof are all artifacts of the same system under review, and the most load-bearing run proof is still an intentionally aborted run. Without visible scanner rules, visible exit-criteria logic, and a successful full E2E run, the package remains more internally consistent than independently verified.

No remaining implementation-level concern that would block this staged pass — the main AI has honestly narrowed scope to what was actually proven and explicitly names what remains open (OL-01, pending OL-06/OL-08, full carrier loop); the safety ceiling, boundary negative test, and OL status honesty are concrete improvements over round 2

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Publish the scanner rules and the open-loop closeout logic so they can be audited. Run the scanner against a diverse set of deliberately contaminated documents. Keep OL-01 open until a full successful complete-revival-e2e run demonstrates retention behavior on the success path. Once those are provided, this stage can be accepted as a valid partial closure.

N/A — this is a staged pass. Future work should: (1) exercise retention after a full carrier_loop run to validate state accumulation doesn't break teardown, (2) define concrete promotion criteria for OL-06/OL-08 from pending-e2e to verified-closed
